unit.why: A short anecdote told by the rebbe: a village miller who recited Psalms all his life is greeted after death by King David, as a tzaddik saw.
unit.boundary_note: The closing remark about the rebbe holding the Warsaw-printed Chumash or Tehillim is a separate aside appended to the tale.

stories.start_quote: וסיפר שפ״א היה איש א׳ העוסק
stories.end_quote: יצא עם כנורו לקראתו והיה מנגן ושמח שמחה גדולה
stories.summary_en: A simple village miller recited Psalms all his days; when he died, a tzaddik saw King David come out with his harp to greet him, playing and rejoicing greatly.

tags.why: The man's lifelong Psalm recitation is the point of the tale.
The man's death is the moment the story turns on.
